accuracy.evidence: Checked against the EYFS statutory framework ELG The Natural World (understand changes in the natural world, including changing states of matter), Development Matters 3 and 4 year olds (talk about the differences between materials and changes they notice), NGSS K-PS3-1 (sunlight warms the Earth's surface) and 2-PS1-4 (some changes from heating or cooling can be reversed). Water freezes at 0 °C, a home freezer runs near −18 °C and a fridge near 4 °C (FSA guidance), so the adult note that a fridge will not make ice is correct. The lab's heat rates keep the order sun > table > freezer, so the race always matches reality.

misconceptions.evidence: Targets the documented early-years ideas about ice and water (Russell, Longden and McGuigan, Nuffield SPACE report on materials; Driver et al. Making Sense of Secondary Science): heat makes ice harder (challenge tag hard), melted ice vanishes (mastery m2), melted ice can never be ice again (prediction in Back to ice, tag never), warmth instead of cold makes ice (tags warm and warmice), all places melt at the same speed (tag same), and snow melting because it got cold or tired (tags cold and tired).

lab_distinct.evidence: flagmelt is a three-place kitchen scene with a running warmth clock: each thing placed in the sunny window, on the table or in the freezer melts or freezes at that place's rate, a cup visibly fills with ice, lollies shrink into puddles, a puddle refreezes, and a job step asks for warm or cold. flagtemp (Temperature and particle motion, 12 to 13) is a particle speed model and gaslab is a gas piston, so nothing here could be relabelled for them. The 30 percent shingle gate passed against every flagship lab.

lab_teaches.evidence: The child finds the rule by doing: ice in the freezer does not melt and the lab says why, water on the table never turns to ice, the three-lolly race shows the warmest place melts first while the table one is still half melted, and the Back to ice step refuses to make ice in the sun before the freezer turns the puddle back. Each done message names the rule only after the child has seen it (Warm made the ice melt into water).

predictions.evidence: Three locked predictions, each with a tempting wrong option the lab disproves: It stays ice for an ice cube in a sunny window (it melts in front of them), Still runny water for a cup in the freezer (it turns to ice), and On the table or In the freezer for which lolly melts first (the sunny one goes first). A.reveal quotes the child's guess in the done message.

challenge_feedback.evidence: Five rotating questions; every wrong answer is tagged and gets its own correction: hard (heat does not make ice harder), nothing (ice in the warm sun melts), warm (warm places melt ice; you need the freezer), never (the puddle turns back into ice), warmice (to make ice it needs cold), same (the warmer the place, the faster), cold and tired (snow is not alive; warm air melts it). Wrong drops in the lab also name the slip, for example The table is not cold enough. Water needs the freezer.

readability.evidence: Kid paragraphs use short read-aloud sentences (Ice is hard. You can hold an ice cube. Ice is a solid.) and pass the family kid limit in validate_lessons. The adult text stays under the family adult limit while using the precise early science terms solid, liquid, melt, freeze, warm (heat), cool, and changes that can be undone (reversible), with the 0 °C freezing point.

no_filler.evidence: The filler gate passed and explanation overlap with every lesson, including Heating and cooling changes and Solids, liquids and gases, is under the 12 percent limit. Each kid paragraph adds one idea (ice is solid, melting, freezing, it goes both ways); the adult paragraphs give the curriculum statements, the key terms with temperatures, four named mistakes and a caution, and the lab outline.

mobile.evidence: Screenshots on iPhone 13 and desktop in dark and light: the three places fill the canvas width as tall boxes (about 120 px each on a 390 px phone) with their names and warm or very cold under each, the ice cube, cup and lolly are about 60 px, the tray sits below for dragging, and the three big buttons (Sunny window, Table, Freezer) are 56 px tall under the canvas. Nothing is clipped; the long label not hot, not cold fits its box.

accessibility.evidence: walk.cjs: axe found no WCAG 2.1 AA violations in light or dark on desktop and iPhone 13, no console or page errors, every Show me completed (5 tasks) and the challenge showed. Every drag has a labelled button twin (Put it in the sunny window, table or freezer), the canvas aria-label speaks each change (The cold freezer froze the water. Now it is hard ice.), and every state has a word label (hard, melting, runny, ice, water) so colour is never the only cue.
